scope: Attribute setup/capture/recognition failures to their source and retain errors reported after recognition drains; no physical device was opened.

changes.diagnostics: Capture failure_source retains the first reported failing source; tracks[].failure_stage retains each track's first reported preparing/capture/recognition stage. Existing capture-level failure_stage remains.
changes.completion: Previously the status loop stopped when the recognition workers reported Finished. Capture callbacks can drop their PCM senders before their thread reports a capture error. The receiver now drains until all capture and recognition status senders close, then joins the workers.
changes.privacy: New fields contain only fixed source/stage labels, never helper paths, input filenames, error text, meeting text or audio.
changes.cancellation: A queued capture cancelled before starting stays stopped with all failure fields null.
changes.reporting: run_jobs reports the final capture error once; both runtime failure scenarios verify exactly one Failed and one CaptureStopped event. This does not count separate device-fallback notices as the same failure.

regression.before: failed: failure_source was null instead of system
regression.after: passes as part of the final regular UI suite

two_sources.command: BOARDCAST_VOICE_DIR=<installed voice models> BOARDCAST_AUTO_AUDIO=<verified shared fixtures> cargo test -p boardcast-ui both_sources_can_recognize_while_the_other_is_waiting -- --ignored
assertions: Successes have no source failure and drain queues.
Each injected runtime failure has system as first failure source and its actual stage.
Each job emits exactly one CaptureStopped; failed scenarios emit exactly one Failed.
Both helpers write their closed marker after EOF.
Diagnostic JSON excludes injected error text and private-missing-audio filename.
two_sources.limitations: Real VAD and SenseVoice language probing with stand-in Apple helpers. CAM++ was unavailable; no speaker embedding or Apple recognition accuracy was measured. The capture-error scenario does not force every possible cross-thread delivery ordering.
